data.templateDescription: Social engagement, light housekeeping, errands. No personal care needs.
data.careGoals:
Reduce isolation through social interaction
Maintain a safe, clean home environment
Assist with errands and appointments
data.specialInstructions:
Activities client enjoys: reading aloud, cards, light walks, music, reminiscing.
Light housekeeping: dishes, laundry, dusting, sweeping.
Meal prep encouraged — eat together when possible.
data.precautions: No major safety concerns. Maintain situational awareness during community outings.
data.medicationNotes: Self-administered. Caregiver does not handle medications.
data.communicationNotes: Engaged conversationalist. Respect privacy on sensitive topics.

data.templateDescription: For clients with moderate cognitive decline. Focus on routine, safety, validation.
data.careGoals:
Maintain consistent daily routine
Minimize agitation and confusion
Ensure home safety (no wandering, no falls)
Provide cognitive engagement
data.specialInstructions:
Same caregiver visits each day if possible — continuity reduces anxiety.
Use validation therapy, not correction. Do not argue about misremembered facts.
Redirect rather than refuse.
Keep environment calm: low noise, soft lighting in evening.
Follow consistent meal/activity/bedtime schedule.
data.precautions:
Wandering risk — verify all doors locked before leaving.
Fall risk — clear pathways, remove throw rugs.
Do not leave client alone with stove on.
Report any new agitation, paranoia, or refusal of care.
data.medicationNotes: Caregiver to remind only. Family/RN administers. Watch for medication refusal — common in dementia.
data.mobilityNotes: Stand-by to minimal assist. Gait may be unsteady — encourage cane/walker use.
data.dietaryNotes: Soft/easy-chew foods preferred if dental issues. Hydrate often — dementia clients often forget to drink.
data.communicationNotes: Speak slowly, one short sentence at a time. Use name. Make eye contact. Avoid open-ended questions; offer simple choices.

data.templateDescription: For diabetic clients needing meal/medication reminders and blood-sugar monitoring.
data.careGoals:
Maintain stable blood glucose
Support diabetic diet adherence
Monitor for signs of hypo/hyperglycemia
Foot/skin daily check
data.specialInstructions:
Remind client to check blood sugar per RN schedule.
Log readings in care notes.
Daily foot inspection — report any wound, redness, or sensation change immediately.
Ensure client eats consistent carb portions at consistent times.
data.precautions:
HYPOGLYCEMIA (BG < 70): glucose tabs/juice, recheck in 15 min, call RN if not resolved.
HYPERGLYCEMIA (BG > 300, fruity breath, confusion): 911.
Any foot wound that doesn't heal in 48h: notify RN.
data.medicationNotes: Insulin / oral hypoglycemics. Caregiver reminds; trained/authorized caregivers may administer per care plan.
data.mobilityNotes: Ambulatory. Avoid hot water for foot soaks (risk of burns with reduced sensation).
data.dietaryNotes: Diabetic / consistent-carb diet. Low sodium if also hypertensive. Limit concentrated sweets.
data.communicationNotes: Alert. Watch for confusion or sluggishness — could indicate blood-sugar swing.

data.templateDescription: Comfort care for terminally ill clients. Comply with hospice plan of care.
data.careGoals:
Maximize comfort and dignity
Support client and family emotionally
Follow hospice plan of care exactly
data.specialInstructions:
Hospice nurse is lead. Caregiver supports, does not direct.
Gentle repositioning q2h to prevent skin breakdown.
Mouth care every 2 hours — terminal dehydration causes dry mouth.
Family presence is comforting — do not interrupt unless asked.
Play favorite music, read aloud, hold hand. Hearing is the last sense to go.
data.precautions:
Do NOT call 911 for expected death — call hospice nurse first.
Do not force food/water — terminal anorexia is natural and not painful.
Any pain or distress: notify hospice immediately.
data.medicationNotes: Comfort meds (morphine, lorazepam, atropine) per hospice. Administered by hospice/family. Caregiver may remind/assist per training.
data.mobilityNotes: Bed-bound likely. Two-person transfer if any. Use draw sheet to reposition.
data.dietaryNotes: Offer small sips/ice chips per tolerance. Do not pressure intake.
data.communicationNotes: May be non-verbal. Continue to speak to client. Identify self when entering room.

data.templateDescription: Bathing, grooming, dressing assistance for a mostly-independent client.
data.careGoals:
Maintain personal hygiene and grooming
Promote dignity and independence
Monitor skin integrity
data.specialInstructions:
Allow client to perform tasks they can manage independently — supervise only.
Offer choices (e.g., shower vs. bath, time of day) to preserve autonomy.
data.precautions:
Watch for skin breakdown around bony prominences.
Report any falls, bruising, or skin changes.
data.medicationNotes: Refer to medication list. Caregiver may remind but not administer unless trained and authorized.
data.mobilityNotes: Ambulatory. Stand-by assistance only — no transfer required unless noted.
data.dietaryNotes: Regular diet. Encourage hydration (8 cups water/day).
data.communicationNotes: Speak clearly, face client. No known communication barriers.

data.templateDescription: Short-term recovery support after orthopedic surgery.
data.frequency: Daily for first 2 weeks, then PRN
data.careGoals:
Promote safe healing per surgeon's instructions
Prevent falls and re-injury
Manage pain comfort
Assist with prescribed PT exercises
data.specialInstructions:
Follow weight-bearing restrictions exactly as ordered (TDWB / PWB / FWB).
Assist with home exercise program — 2x/day at minimum.
Ice 15-20 min after PT exercises.
Elevate surgical leg when resting.
data.precautions:
Watch surgical incision for redness, drainage, swelling — report to RN immediately.
DVT/PE warning signs: calf pain/swelling, sudden shortness of breath — 911.
Do NOT bend hip past 90°, cross legs, or twist (hip clients).
data.medicationNotes: Pain meds usually scheduled. Anticoagulant (e.g., Lovenox, Eliquis) common — watch for bruising/bleeding.
data.mobilityNotes: Use walker for all transfers. Caregiver provides stand-by assist. No bending below knee level (hip restrictions).
data.dietaryNotes: Regular diet. Encourage protein for tissue repair. Hydrate well — anesthesia + opioids cause constipation.
data.communicationNotes: Alert and oriented. Communicate any new pain, fever, or changes promptly.

data.title: Home Care Service Agreement
data.body:
REPLACE THIS TEXT WITH YOUR AGENCY'S OWN SERVICE AGREEMENT BEFORE SENDING IT.

This agreement is between {{AGENCY_NAME}} ("the Agency") and {{CLIENT_NAME}} ("the Client"), beginning {{START_DATE}}.

1. Services. The Agency will provide the services described in the Client's care plan. Services may be adjusted by agreement between the Client and the Agency.

2. Rates and billing. Services are billed at the rate agreed with the Client. Invoices are issued for services delivered.

3. Scheduling and cancellation. The Client will give reasonable notice of a cancellation. The Agency will give notice of any change to a scheduled visit.

4. Caregiver assignment. The Agency assigns caregivers and may substitute a qualified caregiver when the assigned caregiver is unavailable.

5. Termination. Either party may end this agreement with written notice.

By signing, the Client (or their authorised representative) agrees to these terms.

data.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
data.body:
REPLACE THIS TEXT WITH THE RIGHTS STATEMENT REQUIRED IN YOUR STATE BEFORE SENDING IT.

As a client of {{AGENCY_NAME}} you have the right to:
- be treated with dignity and respect
- take part in planning your care and to be told of changes to it
- privacy and confidentiality of your records
- know the name and role of anyone providing your care
- refuse care and be told what that may mean for you
- raise a complaint without it affecting your care

You are responsible for:
- giving accurate information about your health and circumstances
- telling us about changes to your condition, medication or contacts
- providing a safe environment for the people who care for you
- telling us as early as you can when you need to cancel

Signed acknowledgment confirms you have received and understood this statement.

data.title: Notice of Privacy Practices — Acknowledgment
data.body:
REPLACE THIS TEXT WITH YOUR AGENCY'S OWN NOTICE OF PRIVACY PRACTICES ACKNOWLEDGMENT BEFORE SENDING IT.

I acknowledge that I have received the Notice of Privacy Practices of {{AGENCY_NAME}}, which describes how my health information may be used and disclosed and how I can get access to that information.

I understand that {{AGENCY_NAME}} may use and disclose my health information to provide my care, to obtain payment for that care, and for its health care operations.

Acknowledged on {{DATE}}.

data.title: Consent to Care
data.body:
REPLACE THIS TEXT WITH YOUR AGENCY'S OWN CONSENT TO CARE BEFORE SENDING IT.

I consent to receive home care services from {{AGENCY_NAME}} as described in my care plan, beginning {{START_DATE}}.

I understand that:
- I may refuse any service at any time
- my care plan will be reviewed with me and may change as my needs change
- caregivers will document the care they provide

Consent given by {{CLIENT_NAME}} (or their authorised representative) on {{DATE}}.
